topic: Documenting child learning observations with AI assist (without losing your voice)
anecdote: Tried the AI on three individual learning observations for under-5s and deleted all three. The most memorable: I asked it to draft an observation aligned with EYLF Outcome 1 for a 4-year-old who had resolved a peer conflict over a toy in outdoor play. The AI returned a sentence about 'the child demonstrated an emerging capacity for self-regulation and prosocial negotiation strategies.' What I had actually seen was the child looking their friend in the eye and saying 'you can have it after I count to five,' then counting out loud on their fingers. The AI wrote the conclusion. I write the moment. Two things no prompt can give it. First, verbatim child words: a three-year-old saying 'I maked it go faster' tells you something about language development that the phrase 'used descriptive language' erases. Second, the physical detail: which hand they used, whether they leaned in or held back, the three seconds they spent staring at the paint before they touched it. The pause is the learning. My rule now: the AI helps with structure, grammar, and linking language to EYLF outcomes; the observational content stays mine. I write the raw note first, then the AI tightens. I never start with the AI and edit down. If I cannot write at least the core observation myself, I do not publish it.
